class.name: OpenXRMonotonicTimeConversionExtension
class.brief_description: Converts Android suspend-excluding monotonic nanoseconds to OpenXR [code]XrTime[/code].
class.description:
Uses [code]XR_KHR_convert_timespec_time[/code] and the active OpenXR instance. On Android, [method get_android_uptime_nanos] returns the current [code]CLOCK_MONOTONIC[/code] value, equivalent to [code]SystemClock.uptimeNanos()[/code]. The conversion and source timeline both pause during deep sleep.
The integer sentinel [code]-1[/code] means unavailable, invalid, or failed. Conversion requires a positive input and an initialized OpenXR instance. No wall-clock, predicted-display, engine-relative, calibration, or background timing is used.

method.name: is_monotonic_time_conversion_supported
method.description: Returns true only when the extension is enabled for the active instance and its function pointer was resolved.

method.name: get_android_uptime_nanos
method.description: Returns the current Android suspend-excluding monotonic timestamp in nanoseconds, or [code]-1[/code] when unavailable.

method.name: monotonic_nanos_to_xr_time
method.description: Converts the supplied monotonic timestamp without sampling it internally, or returns [code]-1[/code] on invalid input, overflow, unavailable OpenXR, or conversion failure.
